title: How to check a VIN for open recalls (and check a whole fleet at once)
author: CyberMax
summary: A safety recall repair is free at any franchised dealer, but only if someone notices the recall. NHTSA received 958 recall campaigns in the last 12 months (25 September 2025 to 18 September 2026), covering 43,450,237 vehicles and pieces of equipment . 25 of them told owners not to drive the vehicle until it is fixed, and 24 told owners to park outside , away from buildings, because of fire risk. Check one VIN The 17-character VIN is on the driver-side dashboard (visible through the windscreen), the driver's door pillar and the registration and insurance cards. Enter it at nhtsa.gov/recalls . NHTSA shows the recalls that are still open for that exact vehicle , based on what the manufacturer reports. If a recall is open, call any dealer for the brand. The repair is free, even for a used car you bought second-hand. Treat Do Not Drive and Park Outside notices as urgent: those are the ones where the risk is a crash or a fire. What a VIN tells you A VIN decodes to year, make, model, trim, engine and assembly plant. Take the widely used sample VIN 1HGCM82633A004352 : it decodes to a 2003 Honda Accord EX-V6 coupe , 3.0 L six-cylinder, built in Marysville, Ohio. NHTSA lists 24 recall campaigns for the 2003 Accord: 10 for exterior lighting, 9 for front airbag inflators (driver and passenger side) and 5 others. Try it: check VIN 1HGCM82633A004352 (free, no key): curl 'https://recallroll-api.cybermaxtools.com/api/check?vin=1HGCM82633A004352' A model-year lookup is useful even without a VIN: the 2021 Ford F-150 has 29 recall campaigns on file, including one Do Not Drive notice (21V407000, a steering gear that may be damaged internally, fixed by replacing the gear free of charge). A make/model/year recall list shows every campaign that could apply. Whether one specific vehicle is included, or already repaired, is confirmed by VIN at nhtsa.gov or by a dealer. Which makes recall the most Recall campaigns per make, last 12 months Ford 111 Lincoln 32 Toyota 30 Chevrolet 27 Forest River 23 Jeep 23 Altec 22 Hyundai 22 BMW 22 Honda 21 NHTSA campaigns received 25 Sep 2025 to 18 Sep 2026 that name the make. See the per-make pages for models and components, for example Ford, Toyota, Honda and Tesla, or every make. Checking a fleet, a lot or a customer list Typing VINs into a web form works for one car. Dealers checking trade-ins, rental and fleet managers, and insurers need it in a spreadsheet or their own software. title: Unsloth + Ollama: Fine-Tune and Run Local LLMs
author: Marcus Vance | Signal Matrix AI
summary: Unsloth + Ollama: Fine-Tune Open-Source LLMs 2x Faster and Run Them Locally Stop burning thousands of dollars on cloud LLM API tokens. Fine-tuning an 8B parameter model no longer requires a cluster of enterprise A100 GPUs or endless cloud compute budgets. By pairing Unsloth with Ollama , you can perform QLoRA local fine tuning on a consumer GPU using under 8GB of VRAM, convert the model directly to GGUF format, and serve it on your local machine with a single CLI command. Here is how to set up the entire end-to-end pipeline in under 30 minutes. Why Unsloth + Ollama? Standard Hugging Face pipelines often encounter CUDA Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes on 16GB or 24GB GPUs when training 8B parameter models. Unsloth rewrites PyTorch attention layers and cross-entropy loss functions into hand-crafted OpenAI Triton kernels. This optimization yields concrete advantages: 2x Faster Training: Bypasses PyTorch autograd overhead. 70% to 80% Less VRAM: Train Llama 3 8B or Mistral 7B in 6.6GB to 8GB VRAM with QLoRA. Zero Conversion Overhead: Exports directly to quantized GGUF format and auto-generates the Ollama Modelfile . Zero API Bills: Serve your proprietary tuned model locally on macOS, Linux, or Windows via Ollama. Where to Get It (Official Links, GitHub & Hugging Face) Before starting, bookmark and pull resources from the official repositories: Unsloth GitHub Repository: https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth — Core training framework and Triton kernels. Unsloth Official Documentation: https://unsloth.ai/docs — Setup guides, memory benchmarks, and architecture details. Unsloth Hugging Face Hub: https://huggingface.co/unsloth — Official 4-bit pre-quantized base models (Llama 3, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma). Ollama Download: https://ollama.com/download — Standalone installers for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Ollama GitHub Repository: https://github.com/ollama/ollama — Open-source local runtime repository. Quick Install & Setup Set up Ollama and an isolated Python virtual environment on your Linux/WSL2 system with CUDA installed. 1. Install Ollama Runtime curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh 2. Configure Python Virtual Environment Create a dedicated environment and install Unsloth alongside PyTorch dependencies: python3 -m venv finetune-env source finetune-env/bin/activate pip install --upgrade pip pip install 'unsloth[colab-new] @ git+https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth.git' pip install --no-deps trl peft accelerate bitsandbytes datasets How to Use It in Real Life (Step-by-Step Walkthrough) In this walkthrough, we will fine-tune Llama 3 8B Instruct on a customer support dataset, export it to GGUF, and query it locally via Ollama. Step 1: Initialize Model and Adapters Create a training script named train.py . Load the pre-quantized 4-bit model directly from Hugging Face and inject LoRA parameters: import torch from unsloth import FastLanguageModel from datasets import load_dataset from trl import SFTTrainer from transformers import TrainingArguments max_seq_length = 2048 dtype = None # Auto-detect Float16 / Bfloat16 load_in_4bit = True # 1. Load 4-bit base model model , tokenizer = FastLanguageModel . from_pretrained ( model_name = ' unsloth/llama-3-8b-Instruct-bnb-4bit ' , max_seq_length = max_seq_length , dtype = dtype , load_in_4bit = load_in_4bit , ) # 2. Attach LoRA adapters model = FastLanguageModel . get_peft_model ( model , r = 16 , target_modules = [ ' q_proj ' , ' k_proj ' , ' v_proj ' , ' o_proj ' , ' gate_proj ' , ' up_proj ' , ' down_proj ' ], lora_alpha = 16 , lora_dropout = 0 , bias = ' none ' , use_gradient_checkpointing = ' unsloth ' , random_state = 3407 , ) Step 2: Format Data and Train Train on instruction-response pairs using SFTTrainer for 60 steps: # 3. Format dataset using Llama 3 template prompt_template = ''' <|start_header_id|>system<|end_header_id|> You are a specialized internal support bot.<|eot_id|><|start_header_id|>user<|end_header_id|> {}<|eot_id|><|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|> {}<|eot_id|> ''' def formatting_prompts_func ( examples ): texts = [] for instruction , output in zip ( examples [ ' instruction ' ], examples [ ' output ' ]): text = prompt_template . format ( instruction , output ) texts . append ( text ) return { ' text ' : texts } dataset = load_dataset ( ' philschmid/dolly-15k-oai-style ' , split = ' train[:1000] ' ) dataset = dataset . map ( formatting_prompts_func , batched = True ) trainer = SFTTrainer ( model = model , tokenizer = tokenizer , train_dataset = dataset , dataset_text_field = ' text ' , max_seq_length = max_seq_length , dataset_num_proc = 2 , packing = False , args = TrainingArguments ( per_device_train_batch_size = 2 , gradient_accumulation_steps = 4 , warmup_steps = 5 , max_steps = 60 , learning_rate = 2e-4 , fp16 = not torch . cuda . is_bf16_supported (), bf16 = torch . cuda . is_bf16_supported (), logging_steps = 10 , optim = ' adamw_8bit ' , weight_decay = 0.01 , lr_scheduler_type = ' linear ' , seed = 3407 , output_dir = ' outputs ' , ), ) trainer . train () Step 3: Export to GGUF and Ollama Unsloth eliminates manual llama.cpp compilation. Export directly to 4-bit Medium Quantization ( q4_k_m ) at the end of train.py : # 4. Export directly to GGUF model . save_pretrained_gguf ( ' custom_model ' , tokenizer , quantization_method = ' q4_k_m ' ) Run the training file: python train.py This writes the quantized GGUF weights and an automatically configured Modelfile into the ./custom_model directory. Step 4: Register and Run in Ollama Point Ollama to the generated folder and launch the model: # 5. Build and serve inside Ollama ollama create my-assistant -f ./custom_model/Modelfile ollama run my-assistant Example Interaction: >>> How do I reset my company VPN token? To reset your company VPN token: 1. Open the Okta Verify dashboard on your mobile device. 2. Navigate to Settings > Enrolled Factors > VPN Gateway. 3. Click 'Regenerate Token' and confirm your biometric prompt. Your new session token will be active within 60 seconds. Key Takeaways Combining Unsloth and Ollama creates a self-contained local fine-tuning workflow: train locally in 15–30 minutes, eliminate external API dependencies, and keep all proprietary data within your own infrastructure.

title: Reverse Engineer Anything: AI-Powered Binary Analysis

title: ulimit doesn't cap memory on macOS: stop a job before it swaps
author: Rodion Kazennov
summary: On Linux a job's memory can be capped with ulimit -v , systemd-run -p MemoryMax= or a cgroup, and a job that grows too big fails on its own instead of taking the machine down. macOS has no systemd and no cgroups, and ulimit refuses. This is macOS 26.5.2: $ /bin/bash -c 'ulimit -v 1048576' /bin/bash: line 0: ulimit : virtual memory: cannot modify limit: Invalid argument $ /bin/bash -c 'ulimit -m 1048576' /bin/bash: line 0: ulimit : max memory size: cannot modify limit: Invalid argument resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_DATA, ...) in Python raises ValueError , and in the shell where ulimit -m had failed, a script went on to allocate and touch 3 GiB. What macOS does instead is compress memory and write it to swap. A model that doesn't fit doesn't fail: it slows down, and so does everything else on the Mac. So the questions worth asking change: is there room before a job starts, and is swap growing while it runs? Check swap while a job runs sysctl vm.swapusage # compare "used" before and after a run sysctl kern.memorystatus_level # system-wide free memory, in percent The process footprint, the number Activity Monitor shows, doesn't count pages that are already in swap. In one run of Qwen-Image-2.1 with diffusers' model CPU offload on my 48 GB M5 Pro, the footprint never went above 18.5 GB while swap grew by 9.6 GB. A chart of the footprint alone would have called that run a fit. Stop a job before it swaps stageload , a small library I wrote for loading models one stage at a time, ships a guard for this ( pip install stageload ): stageload guard --wait-free 40 --swap-budget 8G -- python generate.py It waits until kern.memorystatus_level is at least 40 %, then starts the command. If swap grows more than 8 GB over what was in use at the start, or free memory stays under 10 % for two samples, it sends SIGTERM to the command's process group and, five seconds later, SIGKILL to whatever is left. It needs no root, and the command and its process group are the only processes it ever stops. Exit code 3 means the guard stopped the command and 4 that it never found room to start it; otherwise you get the command's own exit code. That is how the eager Qwen-Image run ended: it got through all 20 steps, the VAE decode took the footprint to 43.6 GB, swap grew by 8 GB, and the guard stopped it before the Mac stalled. Two heavy jobs at once A guard decides alone. Two guards that find room at the same moment both start their jobs, and each job was sized for a Mac with nothing else running. On 5 October one of my runs started in the gap between two video jobs of another script, and the next video job took swap past its budget within 20 seconds. stageload run puts the jobs in one queue for the machine. It takes the guard's flags. Here two jobs hold 3 and 2 GiB, started from two terminals: stageload run --who images -- python3 alloc.py 3 10 # holds 3 GiB for 10 s stageload run --who upscale -- python3 alloc.py 2 4 # holds 2 GiB for 4 s $ stageload queue ram 0 running images pid 32488 since 2026-10-12T14:08:56+00:00 python3 alloc.py 3 10 ram 1 waiting upscale pid 32499 since 2026-10-12T14:08:58+00:00 python3 alloc.py 2 4 The second job starts when the first one ends, and then the guard's checks run as usual: 14:08:58Z queue: waiting in ram (1 ahead: images) 14:09:08Z queue: start in ram after 10 s, swap 6.0 GB, stop above 14.0 GB or under 10% available twice $ stageload queue --history 2 done ram exit 0 images waited 0 s, ran 10 s, peak 3.0 GB python3 alloc.py 3 10 done ram exit 0 upscale waited 10 s, ran 4 s, peak 2.0 GB python3 alloc.py 2 4 Details that mattered on a shared Mac: Jobs join a lane, ram by default. Lanes don't wait for each other, so a job that waits on a remote API quota can go in a lane of its own ( --lane api --wait-free 0 ) and not hold up the ones that need memory. Turns are fair between owners. The owner who started least recently goes next, so a script that queues twenty jobs takes turns with the others instead of holding the lane. The owner is --owner , or the part of --who before its first dash. Each run writes a memory trace of the command and every process under it, and one line to ~/.stageload/history.jsonl with the wait, the run time, the peak footprint and swap. Engines started outside the queue go in ~/.stageload/busy.txt , one pattern per line. Every run in the ram lane waits until none of them has been seen for 20 seconds. Limits The guard and the meter read macOS counters ( libproc , sysctl ), so they only run on a Mac. The guard stops a job; it doesn't make the job smaller. On the model side, loading one model per stage is what took Qwen-Image-2.1 from 43.6 GB to 19.0 GB on the same Mac: How to run Qwen-Image-2.1 on a 48 GB Mac without swap . For a safety net across the whole machine, macos-oom-guard runs as root and kills the largest process before the kernel panics. The two can run together.

title: WooCommerce Variations Not Showing? A 10-Step Debugging Checklist
author: Amanur Rahman
summary: You add sizes or colors to a WooCommerce product, save it, and open the page. No dropdowns. Or the dropdowns show but a choice is greyed out. Or you get "Sorry, no products matched your selection." After fixing this on many stores, I run the same checks in the same order. Start with settings, then templates and conflicts, then JavaScript and code. Jumping straight to deactivating plugins wastes time. Back up your database and files first, and test on staging if you can. Quick diagnosis What you see Likely cause No dropdowns, only a normal add to cart Product is not set to Variable product Dropdown missing for one attribute Attribute not marked "Used for variations" An option has no price or cannot be selected Variation has no price, is disabled or out of stock "No products matched your selection" Missing combination or variation limit Layout broken after an update Outdated theme template Works logged in, fails for visitors Caching or minification Steps 1 to 4: configuration 1. Product type. In Product data, the dropdown must say Variable product, and the product must be published and visible in the catalog. 2. Attributes. On the Attributes tab, tick "Used for variations" for every attribute you want as a dropdown, then click Save attributes. For global attributes, make sure the terms you need are attached to this product. 3. Each variation. Open the Variations tab and check that every variation is enabled, has a regular price, and has a valid stock status. WooCommerce treats a variation without a price as not purchasable, so it disappears. If you renamed attribute terms after creating variations, delete and regenerate them. 4. Stock settings. Under WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Inventory, check the option that hides out-of-stock items. If every variation is out of stock, the whole product can vanish from the shop. Step 5: "No products matched your selection" Two common causes. First, a missing combination: the customer picked Large and Blue but you only created Large and Red. Second, the variation limit. By default WooCommerce loads variation data in the page for products with up to 30 variations and switches to AJAX above that, which some themes and caching setups handle badly. You can raise the threshold: add_filter ( 'woocommerce_ajax_variation_threshold' , function ( $qty , $product ) { return 100 ; }, 10 , 2 ); Raise it only as far as you need. Very high values make the product page heavier. Steps 6 and 7: templates and conflicts 6. Template overrides. Go to WooCommerce > Status and check the Templates section for outdated overrides. Test with a default theme such as Storefront on staging. If variations appear there, the fix is in your theme or child theme templates. 7. Plugin and builder conflicts. Common culprits are swatch plugins, product table plugins, caching plugins and anything that changes the add-to-cart area. If you built a custom single-product template in a page builder, it must include the Add to Cart element, because that element prints the dropdowns. Deactivate everything except WooCommerce, test, then reactivate one by one. Step 8: JavaScript, caching and minification The dropdowns depend on JavaScript. Open the browser console and reload the page. Red errors mentioning jQuery point to a broken or blocked script. Then purge every cache layer (plugin, host, CDN), pause minify, combine and defer options, and test in a private window. If that fixes it, re-enable optimization with exclusions for jQuery and WooCommerce scripts instead of switching it off everywhere. Step 9: transients and lookup tables Under WooCommerce > Status > Tools, run the tool that clears WooCommerce transients, then run the tools that regenerate the product lookup tables. This fixes wrong price ranges and products missing from filters. On large catalogs, run them at a quiet time. Step 10: read the logs Add these to wp-config.php : define ( 'WP_DEBUG' , true ); define ( 'WP_DEBUG_LOG' , true ); define ( 'WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY' , false ); Reload the product page and check wp-content/debug.log for fatal errors or warnings that name WooCommerce, your theme or a plugin. Turn debugging off afterwards. Prevention Test one variable product on the live site after every update Make changes on staging first Use a child theme instead of editing the parent Retest product pages as a logged-out visitor after changing cache settings FAQ Why does a variation without a price disappear? WooCommerce treats it as not purchasable and hides it or shows an unavailable message. Add a regular price. How many variations can a product have? There is no hard cap, but the default in-page handling stops at 30 and then uses AJAX. Very large numbers can slow the page. Can caching break variation dropdowns? Yes. Combined, minified or delayed JavaScript can stop the script from running, and cached pages can serve stale data. When should I get a developer involved? When you have worked through every step, when the problem started with a theme update, when you need complex options like bundles or conditional fields, or when each day of delay costs sales. I wrote the longer version, with a decision table for DIY versus hiring and more detail on each step, on my site: When WooCommerce Variations Won't Show Up .

title: How to check whether your site blocks ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity
author: David Black
summary: Plenty of sites turn AI crawlers away without anyone having decided to. A security plugin, a CDN setting or a line copied into robots.txt years ago is enough. If an assistant cannot fetch your pages, it cannot quote them, and you will not hear about it. Here is how to check, in about ten minutes. Two kinds of crawler, and why the difference matters AI companies run more than one crawler, and they do different jobs. Answer fetchers read a page so an assistant can answer a question with it, often while someone is waiting: OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User (OpenAI) PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User (Perplexity) Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User (Anthropic) Training crawlers collect pages to train future models: GPTBot (OpenAI) ClaudeBot (Anthropic) CCBot (Common Crawl, whose data many labs use) Google-Extended (a robots.txt token rather than a separate crawler; it controls use of your pages for Gemini) You may reasonably want to block the second group and allow the first. Blocking everything with "AI" in the name is how a business ends up invisible in answers it would have liked to be in. Step 1: read your robots.txt Open https://yourdomain.com/robots.txt in a browser and look for any of the names above. This blocks one crawler from the whole site: User -agent: OAI-SearchBot Disallow: / Things to know while reading it: A crawler obeys the most specific group that names it. If there is a User-agent: GPTBot group, GPTBot ignores the User-agent: * group entirely. Disallow: / blocks everything. Disallow: with nothing after it blocks nothing. A crawler that is never mentioned falls back to the * group, so check that one too. Step 2: check for a block that is not in robots.txt This is the one people miss. Firewalls, bot-protection plugins and CDN "block AI bots" switches refuse requests before robots.txt is ever consulted. Your robots.txt can look fine while every AI request gets a 403. You can get a rough signal by sending a request that identifies itself as a crawler: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} \n " \ -A "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; OAI-SearchBot/1.0)" \ https://yourdomain.com/ A 200 is a good sign. A 403 , 406 or 429 means something in front of your site is refusing that name. Be honest about what this proves. You are not the real crawler, and some protection checks the IP address as well as the name. A refusal here is strong evidence of a block. A 200 is weaker evidence that you are open. Your server or CDN logs are the final word: search them for the crawler names and look at the status codes they actually received. Step 3: decide, then write it down If you want to be quoted in AI answers but not used for training, say so explicitly rather than relying on defaults: User -agent: OAI-SearchBot User -agent: ChatGPT-User User -agent: PerplexityBot User -agent: Perplexity-User User -agent: Claude-SearchBot User -agent: Claude-User Allow : / User -agent: GPTBot User -agent: ClaudeBot User -agent: CCBot User -agent: Google-Extended Disallow: / Then find the setting that caused any firewall block and add the same exceptions there. Changing robots.txt does nothing if the request never gets that far. What this does not do Letting a crawler in means it can read you. It does not mean an assistant will recommend you. That depends on what your pages say and who else says it. A shortcut for step 1 I build MentionMachine, which has a free robots.txt checker for AI crawlers . It reads your file, shows which crawlers are allowed, blocked or never mentioned, and gives you a patch to copy. It writes nothing to your site and needs no account.

Confirm whether the proposed merchant category is supported. A feature seen in a consumer banking application may not be exposed through the merchant API you can access. Source: State Bank of Pakistan — Raast overview Model orders and payments as separate records An order can exist before payment, and one order may receive several payment attempts. Store a unique order reference and the provider’s transaction identifiers. Keep amount and currency explicit. Do not infer a successful payment from a user returning to a success page. Use authenticated provider confirmation or a verified transaction query according to the integration’s documentation. Handle repeated notifications without applying the payment twice. Record state transitions so an operator can see whether a record is pending, confirmed, failed, or reversed. Treat uncertainty as a visible state A timeout does not prove that a payment failed. The provider may have accepted it before the connection dropped. Show a pending state and follow the provider’s approved reconciliation procedure. Retrying a charge blindly can create duplicate-payment disputes. For example, if an order remains pending after a network error, check its referenced transaction before asking the buyer to pay again. Keep that procedure in the support interface. A screenshot can help investigate a complaint, but it should not automatically grant service without verification. Design refunds and daily reconciliation Clarify who may initiate a refund, what evidence is needed, and how the result returns to the order ledger. A refund request and a completed refund should be distinguishable. Restrict consequential actions and preserve an audit record. At a defined cadence, compare provider records with the application’s ledger. Flag unmatched transactions, amount differences, reversals, and pending items beyond the expected window. Give each exception an owner. A successful checkout demonstration does not verify this operational loop. Test the awkward cases before launch Test duplicate notifications, delayed confirmation, interrupted checkout, incorrect amounts, rejected signatures, and concurrent requests. Use the provider’s sandbox and approved test mechanisms. Confirm what happens when support staff cannot immediately obtain a provider response. Document recurring fees and settlement expectations using the provider’s current agreement. Avoid hardcoding a generic percentage found in an old article. The engineering objective is a payment record that staff and customers can trust, even when the happy path fails. Put this into practice Verify merchant capabilities and terms with the provider. Keep order and payment identifiers separate. Authenticate confirmation and handle duplicates. Provide a pending state and a reconciliation procedure. Test refunds, delays, reversals, and mismatched amounts. Frequently asked questions Does Raast mean every app has direct API access? No. Confirm the integration, onboarding, and capabilities available through your participating bank or provider. Can a success redirect prove an order was paid? No. Verify payment through the provider’s supported server-side confirmation or transaction-query mechanism. title: How to Identify Technologies Mentioned in a YouTube Video
author: WgeorgeAssistantIA
summary: "Which technologies does this video talk about?" sounds like a named-entity task, and it is, with a twist: the entities are product names that are short, ambiguous, constantly new and often misheard. This post covers the three problems you meet, and a practical approach to each. Problem 1: what counts as a technology? If you do not decide, the model will. Without a definition you get everything from "JavaScript" to "the cloud" to the presenter's company. Write the definition into the prompt: Include: named products, frameworks, libraries, languages, services, CLIs and protocols Exclude: generic words ("API", "database", "framework"), company names that are not products, channel names, people Then maintain a block list of the noise you actually observe. In our runs, recurring false positives included generic words such as "API" and "Google", and the names of channels. Problem 2: the same tool, many spellings Speakers say "Postgres", "PostgreSQL", "Postgres DB". Captions write "Next JS", "next.js" or "Nexjs". Two things help: Normalise : lower-case, remove spaces and punctuation, strip common suffixes ( js , db ) to create a matching key Keep an alias list for the display name and for deduplication Watch for duplicates that differ by one letter. We saw a tool appear twice because one occurrence was misspelt; a fuzzy match on names within the same video catches it. Translation can also distort names. If your pipeline summarises in another language, instruct the model to keep product names exactly as spoken. A product name turned into a translated phrase is no longer searchable. Problem 3: mentioned does not mean recommended A technology can be: Used in the demo Recommended as an alternative Compared against another Criticised or dismissed Classify the mention type, or at least keep the quote so a reader can judge. This is the difference between a useful tool list and a misleading one. Ambiguous names need context "Neon", "Serena" and "Phantom" are all valid product names, and all share their name with something unrelated. Give the model the surrounding sentence, and when you look up the official site, pass the category as well. A good result for an ambiguous name needs context at both extraction and resolution. Test it on real videos Pick ten videos in your field, run the pipeline and read the list yourself. You will quickly see what kind of noise appears and where the prompt needs a rule. Update the block list and the prompt, run again. Our implementation We built these rules into VidScope , which returns the tools mentioned in a YouTube video with a timestamp and an official link, and avoids returning a link when the match is unclear. FAQ Is this a named-entity recognition problem? Yes, with the twist that names are short, ambiguous and often misheard in captions. How do I stop generic words being returned? Define what counts as a tool in the prompt and keep a block list of observed noise. How do I handle different spellings of the same tool? Normalise names to a matching key and keep an alias list.

title: Fingerprints Are the New Cookies: How Browser Fingerprinting Works and What Developers Should Do About It
author: EME GUG
summary: Hồi trước, muốn track user thì cứ set một cái cookie là xong. Giờ thì khác rồi: Safari có ITP, Firefox có Total Cookie Protection, Chrome cũng siết third-party cookie, user thì bấm "Reject all" ngay khi thấy cookie banner. Nhưng tracking không biến mất, nó chỉ chuyển sang chỗ khác: browser fingerprinting . Không cần lưu gì trên máy user, chỉ cần gom đủ tín hiệu từ trình duyệt là có thể nhận ra một người với độ chính xác khá cao, kể cả khi họ dùng Incognito. Bài này mình không viết để dạy track người khác. Mục tiêu là để dev Việt hiểu cơ chế, biết code của mình (hoặc SDK bên thứ ba mình nhúng vào) đang làm gì, và dùng fingerprinting đúng chỗ: chống fraud, chống bot, phát hiện account takeover. Không dùng để quảng cáo lén. Fingerprint được tạo ra từ đâu? Ý tưởng cốt lõi rất đơn giản: mỗi thuộc tính riêng lẻ thì nhiều người trùng nhau, nhưng ghép 20-30 thuộc tính lại thì tổ hợp gần như là duy nhất. Nghiên cứu Panopticlick của EFF từ năm 2010 đã cho thấy khoảng 83% trình duyệt có fingerprint unique, và đến giờ con số đó chỉ có tăng. Các nhóm tín hiệu phổ biến: Passive (server thấy luôn) : IP, User-Agent , Accept-Language , thứ tự HTTP header, TLS ClientHello (JA3/JA4), HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame. Active (cần chạy JS) : Canvas rendering, WebGL renderer/vendor, AudioContext, danh sách font, screen.width/height , devicePixelRatio , hardwareConcurrency , timezone, navigator.languages . flowchart LR A[Browser] -->|TLS ClientHello| B[JA4 hash] A -->|HTTP headers| C[Header fingerprint] A -->|JS chạy trên trang| D[Canvas / WebGL / Audio] A -->|JS| E[Screen, fonts, timezone] B --> F[Combine + hash] C --> F D --> F E --> F F --> G[Visitor ID] Điểm đáng sợ nhất là canvas fingerprint: cùng một đoạn vẽ text + gradient, nhưng GPU, driver, font rendering, anti-aliasing khác nhau sẽ ra pixel khác nhau. Hash cái output đó lại là có một ID khá ổn định. Tự viết một fingerprint đơn giản bằng JavaScript Đoạn dưới đây chạy được trên Chrome 120+, Firefox 120+, Safari 17+. Mình dùng crypto.subtle có sẵn, không cần thư viện: async function sha256 ( text ) { const buf = await crypto . subtle . digest ( ' SHA-256 ' , new TextEncoder (). encode ( text )); return [... new Uint8Array ( buf )]. map ( b => b . toString ( 16 ). padStart ( 2 , ' 0 ' )). join ( '' ); } function canvasSignal () { const c = document . createElement ( ' canvas ' ); c . width = 240 ; c . height = 60 ; const ctx = c . getContext ( ' 2d ' ); ctx . textBaseline = ' top ' ; ctx . font = ' 16px Arial ' ; ctx . fillStyle = ' #f60 ' ; ctx . fillRect ( 100 , 1 , 62 , 20 ); ctx . fillStyle = ' #069 ' ; ctx . fillText ( ' Xin chào, fingerprint 🍜 ' , 2 , 15 ); return c . toDataURL (); } function webglSignal () { const gl = document . createElement ( ' canvas ' ). getContext ( ' webgl ' ); if ( ! gl ) return ' no-webgl ' ; const ext = gl . getExtension ( ' WEBGL_debug_renderer_info ' ); return ext ? gl . getParameter ( ext . UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL ) : ' masked ' ; } async function getFingerprint () { const signals = { ua : navigator . userAgent , langs : navigator . languages . join ( ' , ' ), tz : Intl . DateTimeFormat (). resolvedOptions (). timeZone , screen : ` ${ screen . width } x ${ screen . height } @ ${ devicePixelRatio } ` , cores : navigator . hardwareConcurrency , canvas : await sha256 ( canvasSignal ()), webgl : webglSignal (), }; return { id : await sha256 ( JSON . stringify ( signals )), signals }; } getFingerprint (). then ( fp => console . table ( fp . signals )); Mở Chrome thường rồi mở Incognito, chạy lại: bạn sẽ thấy id y hệt nhau. Đó chính là lý do người ta nói fingerprint là cookie mới, chỉ khác là user không xóa được. Thử trên Firefox với privacy.resistFingerprinting = true trong about:config , hoặc trên Brave/Tor Browser: canvas sẽ bị thêm noise hoặc trả về dữ liệu chuẩn hóa, timezone thành UTC, screen size bị làm tròn. ID sẽ đổi mỗi session hoặc trùng với hàng nghìn người khác. Phía server: passive fingerprint không cần JavaScript Nhiều bot dùng headless browser nên JS fingerprint có thể bị giả. Server-side fingerprint khó giả hơn vì nó nằm ở tầng network. Ví dụ đơn giản với FastAPI 0.115, gom các header và thứ tự của chúng: import hashlib from fastapi import FastAPI , Request app = FastAPI () SIGNAL_HEADERS = [ ' user-agent ' , ' accept ' , ' accept-language ' , ' accept-encoding ' , ' sec-ch-ua ' , ' sec-ch-ua-platform ' , ' sec-fetch-site ' ] @app.middleware ( ' http ' ) async def passive_fp ( request : Request , call_next ): # Thứ tự header raw là tín hiệu rất mạnh: curl, requests, Chrome đều khác nhau order = ' , ' . join ( k . decode (). lower () for k , _ in request . scope [ ' headers ' ]) values = ' | ' . join ( request . headers . get ( h , ' - ' ) for h in SIGNAL_HEADERS ) ja4 = request . headers . get ( ' x-ja4 ' , ' - ' ) # do reverse proxy gắn vào raw = f ' { order } # { values } # { ja4 } ' request . state . fp = hashlib . sha256 ( raw . encode ()). hexdigest ()[: 16 ] # Chrome thật luôn gửi sec-ch-ua; UA nói là Chrome mà thiếu thì đáng nghi ua = request . headers . get ( ' user-agent ' , '' ) request . state . suspicious = ' Chrome/ ' in ua and ' sec-ch-ua ' not in request . headers return await call_next ( request ) @app.get ( ' /whoami ' ) async def whoami ( request : Request ): return { ' fp ' : request . state . fp , ' suspicious ' : request . state . suspicious } Test nhanh bằng curl để thấy sự khác biệt: # curl giả UA Chrome nhưng thiếu client hints -> suspicious = true curl -s -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0) Chrome/129.0 Safari/537.36' \ http://localhost:8000/whoami # Xem TLS fingerprint của chính bạn (cần curl 8.x) curl -sv https://localhost:8443 2>&1 | grep -E 'TLS|ALPN' JA4 (bản kế nhiệm JA3, do FoxIO công bố năm 2023) hash các thông tin trong TLS ClientHello như cipher suites, extensions, ALPN. Python requests có JA4 khác hẳn Chrome, nên dù bot có giả User-Agent hoàn hảo thì tầng TLS vẫn lộ. Nginx có module, HAProxy 3.x và nhiều CDN đã hỗ trợ tính JA4 rồi gắn vào header cho backend. sequenceDiagram participant C as Client participant P as Reverse Proxy participant A as App participant R as Risk Engine C->>P: TLS ClientHello P->>P: Tính JA4 C->>P: HTTP request + headers P->>A: Forward + x-ja4 A->>R: fp + JS fingerprint + IP R-->>A: score (allow / challenge / block) A-->>C: Response hoặc CAPTCHA Dùng đúng chỗ: fraud, không phải tracking Đây là phần dev hay bỏ qua. Ở Việt Nam, Nghị định 13/2023/NĐ-CP về bảo vệ dữ liệu cá nhân đã có hiệu lực, và Luật Bảo vệ dữ liệu cá nhân 2025 tiếp tục siết chặt hơn. Ở EU thì GDPR và ePrivacy Directive coi fingerprinting là xử lý dữ liệu cá nhân, cần consent giống hệt cookie. Nếu sản phẩm của bạn có user châu Âu thì đừng nghĩ fingerprint là cách lách cookie banner. Vài nguyên tắc mình áp dụng: Purpose limitation : chỉ dùng fingerprint ở các flow nhạy cảm như login, checkout, đổi mật khẩu, tạo tài khoản hàng loạt. Không gửi sang analytics hay ad network. Fingerprint là tín hiệu, không phải danh tính : dùng như một input cho risk score. Fingerprint mới + IP lạ + đăng nhập lúc 3h sáng thì mới bật 2FA challenge, đừng block cứng chỉ vì fingerprint đổi. Retention ngắn : lưu hash, đặt TTL 30-90 ngày, không lưu raw canvas data. Audit SDK bên thứ ba : mở DevTools, tab Network/Sources, search toDataURL , getImageData , UNMASKED_RENDERER , OfflineAudioContext . Nhiều SDK chat, analytics, A/B testing đang fingerprint user mà team không biết. Đừng phạt user quan tâm privacy : người dùng Brave, Firefox RFP, Safari sẽ có fingerprint thay đổi liên tục. Nếu hệ thống coi đó là bot thì bạn đang chặn nhầm chính những user cẩn thận nhất. Kết luận Cookie đang chết dần, fingerprinting đang lên, và nó vô hình với user hơn nhiều. Là developer, bạn nên: Hiểu cơ chế : chạy đoạn JS ở trên trên vài trình duyệt khác nhau, so sánh kết quả để thấy tận mắt độ ổn định của từng tín hiệu. Kết hợp nhiều tầng : JS fingerprint dễ giả, header và JA4 ở tầng network khó giả hơn. Dùng cả hai cho bài toán chống bot. Audit code và SDK : grep codebase và bundle production tìm các API canvas, WebGL, audio. Biết chính xác ai đang thu thập gì. Tuân thủ pháp lý : coi fingerprint là dữ liệu cá nhân, ghi rõ trong privacy policy, xin consent khi cần, đặt TTL. Test với trình duyệt privacy-focused : đảm bảo Firefox RFP, Brave, Safari không bị hệ thống chống fraud của bạn chặn nhầm. Fingerprinting là con dao hai lưỡi. Dùng để chặn credential stuffing thì rất hiệu quả, còn dùng để theo dõi user khắp nơi thì sớm muộn cũng bị trình duyệt chặn, bị luật phạt, và mất niềm tin của user.

title: I'm Building a School-Life RPG Where 300 Students Have Lives of Their Own
author: Ferdo Vukojević
summary: I've been working on a personal project called The Merit Academy , a single-player, anime-inspired school-life RPG where you enrol at an elite academy, attend classes, take exams, build relationships, and try to make something of yourself over the course of your school life. It's heavily inspired by the kind of social strategy and academic competition you see in Classroom of the Elite , but I'm building it as its own game, with its own world and identity. The project is still early in development, but I wanted to start sharing what I'm working on, why I'm building it, and some of the challenges involved. The idea I've always liked games where the world feels like it exists independently of the player. That's the main thing I'm trying to achieve with The Merit Academy. Imagine walking through campus on a Monday morning. Some students are heading to class, others are studying in the library, and a few are probably skipping lessons entirely. You might run into someone you spoke to yesterday, but they aren't standing in the same spot waiting for you to interact with them. They have their own schedules, interests, relationships, and things to do. That's the experience I'm trying to build. A campus that changes with time One of the things I've been working on is the academy itself. The campus includes academic buildings, student facilities, sports areas, and places where students can spend their free time. I also wanted the environment to change throughout the year. Spring brings cherry blossoms, autumn changes the colours of the campus, winter covers everything in snow, and rainy days give the whole place a different atmosphere. It's a relatively small detail compared to the gameplay systems, but I think it makes a huge difference when you're spending dozens of hours in the same world. Below are some early looks at the academy across different seasons. [Insert the four-season campus image here] Making NPCs feel like actual students This is probably the most interesting challenge in the project. I'm working toward a system that can support hundreds of students without making the campus feel overcrowded or turning every NPC into someone who just stands around waiting for the player. The idea is that students have routines based on their personalities, interests, and responsibilities. Someone who's serious about academics might spend more time in the library. An athlete might head to practice after class. Others might hang out with friends or visit different campus facilities. Not everyone needs to be visible on the map at the same time. And if you arrange to meet someone somewhere, their schedule should account for that. I'm still developing and refining these systems, but getting this right is one of my biggest priorities. School should actually feel like school Another thing I wanted to avoid was making lessons and exams feel like buttons you click to increase a stat. I want studying to mean something. When you attend a lesson, you should have opportunities to learn, answer questions, and prepare for future exams. If you tutor another student, you should actually help them understand the material rather than simply clicking a "Tutor" button and watching their academic ability increase. The same applies to relationships. Conversations shouldn't just be a way to collect relationship points. Your answers, the context, and the personality of the person you're speaking to should all matter. The goal is to make the different systems feel connected rather than like separate minigames. The technical challenge I'm a software developer by profession, but building a game with interconnected simulation systems is a different kind of challenge. There are quite a few things I'm working through: Simulating student schedules without unnecessarily rendering hundreds of characters. Keeping track of relationships, reputation, and decisions over time. Making academic progression meaningful without turning it into a repetitive grind. Connecting NPC behaviour with story events and player interactions. Keeping the game responsive as more systems and characters are introduced. One of the things I've learned is that adding a feature is often easier than making it interact naturally with everything else. A simple decision like meeting another student after class can affect schedules, relationships, dialogue, locations, and potentially future events. That's where things get interesting. Where the project stands The Merit Academy is being developed independently, and there's no release date yet. I'm still building and improving the foundations, experimenting with gameplay systems, and figuring out what works. Some features are already implemented, some are being reworked, and others are still ideas I want to explore. I'm trying to be transparent about that rather than presenting every planned feature as something that's already playable. Following the development I've started documenting the project publicly, including the things that work, the things that don't, and what I'm planning next. If you're interested, you can follow along here: 🌐 Website and development journal: https://www.ferdo-vukojevic.com/the-merit-academy 📸 Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/tma_meritacademy/ ❤️ Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/c/TheMeritAcademy The website has the full project overview, roadmap, and gallery. Instagram is where I'll share shorter updates, screenshots, and gameplay previews, while Patreon is there for anyone who wants to support development and follow the process more closely. I'd love to hear your thoughts If you were playing a school-life RPG, what would make the academy feel alive to you? Would it be the NPC routines, meaningful relationships, academic competition, unexpected events, or something else entirely? I'm particularly interested in hearing from other developers who've worked on NPC scheduling, simulation systems, or games with large numbers of interacting characters. There's still a lot to build, but I'm enjoying the process and looking forward to sharing more of it. Thanks for reading!

title: Flutter + NVIDIA Edge AI: Model Versioning and Runtime Capability Negotiation
author: vmodal_ai
summary: Flutter + NVIDIA Edge AI: Model Versioning and Runtime Capability Negotiation This advanced tutorial treats Flutter as the operator-facing presentation layer while wearable SDKs, Jetson services, ROS 2 nodes, and NVIDIA-accelerated inference handle device-specific or compute-heavy work. The goal is predictable latency, bounded memory, useful observability, and graceful degradation—not simply maximizing message throughput. Architecture note: Keep safety-critical control loops on the robot. A Flutter app is not a hard real-time controller and must not be the sole safety mechanism. 1. Define measurable service objectives Track freshness, event-to-display latency, throughput, frame pacing, CPU, memory, network use, battery, thermal state, dropped messages, reconnect time, and command acknowledgements. Do not use a single FPS number to represent the entire system: a smooth screen can still display stale data. 2. Instrument the complete path sensor capture -> native/ROS processing -> gateway publish -> Flutter receive -> state accepted -> widget build -> frame rendered Record source and receive timestamps separately. Use monotonic clocks for elapsed durations within a process. When comparing devices, account for clock offset and uncertainty. Profile on a physical target in profile mode and inspect Flutter DevTools' Performance view. Debug-mode timing is not a reliable production baseline. See https://docs.flutter.dev/tools/devtools/performance 3. Establish a repeatable baseline Start from a clean launch. Connect to the robot or replay a fixed trace. Run a representative scenario for several minutes. Record frame times, memory, CPU, message rates, stale-data counts, and reconnects. Change one variable at a time. Compare p50, p95, and p99 latency, not just averages. class PipelineMetrics { int received = 0 ; int accepted = 0 ; int dropped = 0 ; int stale = 0 ; int uiPublishes = 0 ; } Use bounded metric windows or histograms; do not store every sample forever. 4. Separate acquisition from presentation High-rate sources should not directly trigger widget rebuilds. Use a latest-value cache for state-like data, bounded queues for events that must be preserved, and a controlled presentation cadence. class LatestValue < T > { T ? _value ; int _version = 0 ; void put ( T value ) { _value = value ; _version ++ ; } T ? get value = > _value ; int get version = > _version ; } Replacing an older pending value may be acceptable for battery, pose, or temperature. Commands, alarms, and audit events need a separate reliable path and explicit acknowledgement semantics. 5. Make buffering bounded Every queue needs a maximum capacity, an overflow policy, a drop/replacement counter, and an owner responsible for recovery. Latest wins: pose, preview frames, current detections. Drop old items: display-oriented streams where freshness matters. Persist: events that must survive disconnection. Reject with feedback: commands that cannot safely be queued. An unbounded telemetry or log list turns overload into memory growth rather than a visible, measurable condition. 6. Protect the Flutter frame budget Keep parsing, filtering, and transformations out of build() . Split screens into independently updating sections and avoid rebuilding camera or map widgets for unrelated state changes. For CPU-heavy pure Dart work, benchmark compute or a dedicated isolate with realistic payload sizes. Isolates have startup and message-transfer costs. For hardware acceleration or platform APIs, prefer a native service designed for that workload. 7. Keep robotics compute near the robot Sensors -> ROS 2 / accelerated nodes -> Jetson gateway | compact UI-facing state | WebSocket / MQTT / gRPC | Flutter client NVIDIA Isaac ROS provides accelerated, low-latency ROS 2 packages for Jetson and other NVIDIA platforms. Keep image processing, inference, and robot control on the compute side; send Flutter only the information needed for visualization and operator decisions. See https://nvidia-isaac-ros.github.io/ 8. Treat stale data as a first-class state Carry source timestamp, receive timestamp, sequence number/version, source identity, and optional confidence or quality. The UI must distinguish zero from unknown, disconnected, and stale. Do not show a green health indicator just because the last payload was healthy. 9. Validate graceful degradation Simulate network delay and packet loss, bursts, robot process restarts, wearable permission loss, camera interruptions, inference slowdown, low memory, and thermal throttling. Under pressure, reduce preview resolution or update frequency and pause nonessential charts—but preserve command and safety status visibility. 10. Release checklist [ ] Frame-time baseline captured on physical hardware [ ] p50/p95/p99 event-to-display latency measured [ ] Queues bounded and overflow observable [ ] High-frequency state coalesced before UI updates [ ] Commands and alarms use reliable semantics [ ] Clock domains and stale-data rules documented [ ] Network and reconnect behavior tested [ ] Thermal and memory pressure scenarios tested [ ] Robot safety remains independent of the mobile app [ ] Performance budgets enforced in repeatable tests Advanced focus: Model capability negotiation Expose model name/version, supported classes, input resolution, coordinate format, and optional capabilities through a gateway manifest. Adapt the UI to the actual capabilities instead of assuming every robot runs the same model. Keep model deployment and inference on Jetson unless on-device Flutter inference is an explicit requirement. Implementation exercise Add timestamps and sequence IDs at the gateway boundary. Capture a normal-load trace and a burst-load trace. Implement a bounded buffer and an explicit overload policy. Display stale/disconnected/degraded states separately. Profile on the target device and compare p50, p95, and p99 results. Document which events may be coalesced and which must be preserved. Conclusion The strongest performance gains usually come from controlling the whole data pipeline: acquisition, processing, filtering, transport, state updates, and rendering. Keep compute close to the hardware, bound every queue, measure freshness as well as frame rate, and keep safety-critical behavior independent of the Flutter client. title: Build a Delivery AI Agent with MCP and Routing APIs
author: JustRouting
summary: AI agents are getting better at understanding requests, reasoning about problems, and completing complex tasks. But real-world operations need more than language. A delivery assistant needs to answer questions like: Which driver should handle this order? How long will delivery take? What is the most efficient route? How should multiple vehicles be assigned? These are not text problems. They are routing problems. In this tutorial, we will build a delivery AI agent that uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to access routing capabilities. The agent will be able to: convert addresses into coordinates compare drivers by travel time calculate routes optimize multiple deliveries The final architecture: flowchart TD U[User Request] --> A[AI Agent] A --> M[MCP Server] M --> G[Geocoding] M --> R[Routing] M --> O[Optimization] G --> J[JustRouting API] R --> J O --> J The stack: MCP for connecting AI agents with tools JustRouting MCP server for routing capabilities Southeast Asia routing data Why delivery agents need routing tools A language model can understand: "Which driver should deliver this order?" But it does not know: road distances travel times geographic relationships delivery optimization The AI agent decides what to do. The routing system calculates what is physically possible. LLM = reasoning Routing engine = transportation intelligence This separation is important. The AI agent handles: user intent business rules decision making The routing layer handles: maps distances travel time optimization Install the MCP routing server JustRouting provides an MCP server that exposes Southeast Asia routing capabilities to AI clients. Install: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justrouting/mcp/main/install.sh | sh Configure your MCP client: { "mcpServers" : { "justrouting" : { "command" : "justrouting-mcp" , "env" : { "JUSTROUTING_API_KEY" : "YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } The MCP server provides four tools: Tool Purpose geocode Convert addresses into coordinates route Calculate routes table Compare travel times optimize Plan vehicle routes Example 1: Assign the closest driver A dispatcher asks: Assign the closest driver to Mondrian Singapore Duxton. Available drivers: D1: Marina Bay Sands D2: Waterford Residence D3: IKEA Alexandra D4: VivoCity The AI agent creates a workflow: flowchart LR A[Customer Address] --> B[Geocode] B --> C[Calculate Travel Times] C --> D[Compare Drivers] D --> E[Recommend Driver] The routing result: Driver Location Distance Drive time D1 Marina Bay Sands 3.60 km ~8 min D2 Waterford Residence 2.78 km ~6 min D3 IKEA Alexandra 5.33 km ~13 min D4 VivoCity 3.30 km ~7 min The agent responds: Assign D2. Reason: - Shortest driving distance: 2.78 km - Estimated arrival: ~6 minutes The AI agent handles the business question: "Who should deliver this order?" The routing layer provides the transportation intelligence: "These are the actual driving costs." Example 2: Route planning A user asks: How long does it take to drive from Marina Bay Sands Singapore to Changi Airport? The AI agent calls the route tool. Result: Distance: ~19.1 km Duration: ~23 minutes Main roads: East Coast Parkway Airport Boulevard The agent can explain: The fastest driving route takes about 23 minutes. The route uses ECP and Airport Boulevard. ERP charges may apply. The user asks: What if I'm riding a motorcycle? The agent changes routing profiles: Car: Distance: ~19.1 km Time: ~23.6 min Motorcycle: Distance: ~19.1 km Time: ~26.5 min The user adds: What if I want to avoid tolls? The agent applies a routing constraint: Motorcycle with tolls: Distance: ~19.1 km Time: ~26.5 min Motorcycle without tolls: Distance: ~21.6 km Time: ~35 min The AI agent understands: "drive" → driving profile "motorcycle" → motorcycle profile "avoid tolls" → routing constraint The routing layer handles the geography. Example 3: Fleet optimization Single-driver dispatch is useful. But real logistics problems are more complex. A dispatcher asks: I have two vans and six pickup locations. Create today's routes. Vehicles: V1: 249 Sixth Ave, Singapore V2: 8 Harlyn Rd, Singapore Customers: C1: 75 Jln Kelabu Asap C2: 20 Mount Sinai Rd C3: 10 Bin Tong Park C4: 9 Cluny Park C5: 28 Nassim Rd C6: 30 Chancery Ln The AI agent calls: optimize The optimization engine returns: Van V1 Start: 249 Sixth Ave Route: C2 → C1 → C3 Total: ~19.4 minutes and: Van V2 Start: 8 Harlyn Rd Route: C6 → C5 → C4 Total: ~29.0 minutes Final answer: All six deliveries assigned. No customer left unserved. Combined fleet driving time: ~48.5 minutes. The AI agent does not manually solve the vehicle routing problem. It delegates mathematical optimization to a specialized routing engine. The complete delivery AI architecture flowchart TD U[User] --> A[AI Agent] A --> M[MCP Server] M --> G[Geocode] M --> R[Route] M --> T[Travel Time Matrix] M --> O[Optimize] G --> J[JustRouting] R --> J T --> J O --> J Each component has a clear responsibility. AI Agent Understands: user requests business rules priorities MCP Provides: standardized tool access discoverable capabilities Routing API Handles: maps distances travel times optimization Why MCP changes application architecture Before MCP: AI application | Custom integration | External services Every AI application needs to build its own connectors. With MCP: flowchart TD A[AI Application] --> M[MCP Tools] M --> C[Reusable Capabilities] C --> R[Routing] C --> S[Search] C --> P[Payments] A routing server becomes a reusable capability that can be used by: delivery agents fleet assistants travel planners field service systems logistics copilots Beyond delivery The same pattern applies to many physical-world applications. Ride-hailing Question: Which driver should accept this passenger? Needs: geocoding ETA calculation distance comparison Field service Question: Which technician should visit this customer? Needs: location matching scheduling routing Emergency response Question: Which vehicle can arrive fastest? Needs: route calculation travel-time estimation Build AI applications that understand the physical world Large language models provide reasoning. MCP provides tool access. Routing provides location intelligence. Together they enable AI systems that can make decisions in the real world. A delivery AI agent is not just a chatbot. It is a system that can: understand a request call specialized tools evaluate options take action The next generation of logistics software will not only show routes. It will reason about movement.
